_doc: Which frontend pages the capture gate scores against retail, and how badly
each is allowed to do before the gate FAILS. Consumed by
regressionCeiling is a REGRESSION CEILING, NOT A PARITY CLAIM. Every entry
sits above a `measured` value recorded beside it, and several of those
measured values are enormous - title-logo and bg-emblem-topright are both
wrong by a third of their area (task #17). The ceiling says 'do not get
worse than this'. It does not say the page is right. Anyone quoting a
ceiling as a parity number is misreading the file.
The gated statistic is gapPct: pixels where we differ materially from the
retail reference AND retail's own second run does not. Per-pixel and
floor-aware, so animated content retail cannot reproduce itself is not
charged to us, while a layer we never drew still is.
Ceilings are applied to the WORST sample, never the mean - a regression
visible at one video phase is still a regression.
_referenceNote: The no-skipfmv two-run set. -skipfmv degrades the main menu itself by
84.18% material, so the older -skipfmv reference could not be used for

captureDeterminism: Two full mainmenu captures of 684c7c52 taken back to back were
byte-identical on all 161 frames. Our own contribution to run-to-run
variance is 0.00%, so the 2.00pp margin below is entirely headroom
against incidental change, not an allowance for our own flake.

_windowNote: FEP_MAIN is gated as THREE windows rather than one, because retail builds
the page up in stages and a single window would hide a regression behind
the stage we are worst at.
Measured 2026-07-27 from the retail run1 burst, region mean RGB:
t000014  lang-selector, menu-column and the arcs are ALL exactly the
flat fill (23,23,48). Only title-logo and bg-emblem-topright
are drawn. Retail's first main-menu frame carries background
plus logo plus emblem and NOTHING ELSE.
t000524  all chrome present and over-bright (lang-selector 66,82,122)
t001020+ settling to its steady value (lang-selector 58,52,74)
We draw the entire page on frame 0, which is why the entry window scores
76% gap against a retail cross-run floor of 0.24% - retail is perfectly
reproducible there and we simply differ. That is a real defect, tracked
separately; it is NOT a capture artefact and must not be excluded to make
the numbers look better. Gating it in its own window keeps it visible and
keeps the settled window sensitive at its own ~20% scale.

_samplesNote: Every settled retail run1 burst offset, not the five the hand
measurements used. The extra seven cost a few seconds and they are
the ones that would catch a phase regression that happens to look
fine at the five offsets a human picked.

unscored.reason: retail's own two runs disagree by 5.8-44.2% material at matched page-entry offsets, so no reconstruction improvement below that is measurable. Gating on it would be theatre.
retail's own two runs disagree by 9.6-62.5% material; best-match offset drifts by a near-constant -2.0 s whose mechanism is not established.
